stem:
The diagram shows quadrilateral $ABCD$ with both pairs of opposite sides parallel. Sameer asks how rectangles and squares relate to parallelograms.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: $ABCD$ is a parallelogram; rectangles and squares are special parallelograms because their opposite sides are parallel.
$ABCD$ is a parallelogram only if all four angles are $90^{\circ}$.
The same rule classifies any open broken line of four segments as a parallelogram.

teacher.key_rationale: Both pairs of opposite sides parallel make a parallelogram; rectangles and squares sit inside that set. Requiring four right angles adds an unneeded condition. Saying every parallelogram is a rectangle reverses the inclusion. Open polylines are outside the closed-quadrilateral scope.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source as parallelogram ABCD with opposite sides parallel.
